key_insight: A data-free, continuous-time PINN generates cylinder vortex shedding, while enforcing pressure continuity and a hidden incompressibility constraint improves consistency across time windows.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports reference-data-free prediction of unsteady wakes and aerodynamic loads, reducing artificial jumps in lift between training windows.
method: Train a continuous-time PINN over successive time windows without temporal discretization.
Trigger shedding using an analytical, divergence-free initial condition that breaks wake symmetry.
Enforce junction pressure and add the hidden constraint ∇·∂ₜv = 0 to the loss.
evidence_signal: At Re=100, the Strouhal number and mean drag agree with same-domain OpenFOAM results within 0.5%; over five shedding periods, the remedy reduces lift jumps 20-fold.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to the reported Re=100 cylinder case; pressure continuity alone does not ensure dynamically consistent window transitions.
paper_title: Data-free continuous-time physics-informed neural networks for vortex shedding: a consistent pressure across time windows
